title: Verify qsi.4: does wc_HmacSetKey skip software key validation when SETKEY callback returns 0?
description: qsi.4 (HMAC key < 14 bytes accepted) severity depends on whether wolfSSL runs its own key-length validation even when the SETKEY callback returns 0. Read wolfcrypt/src/hmac.c, wc_HmacSetKey: trace the WOLF_CRYPTO_CB_SETKEY path. If callback returns 0 (not CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE), does wolfSSL: (a) return 0 early without running its own key size check? (b) OR run the check anyway? If (a): qsi.4 is confirmed — a 10-byte HMAC key bypasses wolfSSL FIPS validation entirely and lands on hardware. If (b): qsi.4 severity is lower — wolfSSL catches short keys before they reach hardware in FIPS mode. Update qsi.4 description with the finding.
